to: Dicklesworthstone/destructive_command_guard maintainers or commercial team via the repository's public contact route
subject: Bounded ai-agents integration pilot for Dicklesworthstone/destructive_command_guard
body:
Hello destructive_command_guard maintainers,

Unsolicited note about dcg — this is a speculative paid-pilot approach, not a claim you advertised a contract. The repo purpose (blocking dangerous git and shell commands from being executed by agents) is a category I care about specifically because most agent loops today only find out a `rm -rf` or a force push slipped through when a downstream user reports the damage; the Rust CLI shape here is exactly the right substrate to lean on for a strict, testable guard. That's the wedge for a bounded paid pilot: I pick one concrete adjacent surface — a Claude Code / Codex / agent-loop harness that currently doesn't invoke dcg, or an existing dangerous-command rule that lacks a red-team fixture — and ship a minimal integration plus a failing-case test, with an exportable JSON receipt of the invocations that ran and were blocked.

Proposed first milestone (paid, fixed-scope):
1. Pick one agent loop or one rule class dcg does not yet guard.
2. Ship the integration + a failing-case fixture that dcg blocks, with a receipt.
3. Hand over the patch, a short maintainer runbook, and one acceptance check maintainers can re-run.

Proof: https://hfo-games.pages.dev/ ships 21 live browser games and https://github.com/TTaoGaming/hfo-gen-133 exposes the append-only receipt / operator-gated effect model I use — same shape of auditability dcg exists to enforce, applied to my own workflow. Integration labor, not a maintainer role ask.

If that surface is real, book 15 minutes: {{OPERATOR_BOOKING_LINK}}. Otherwise no follow-up.

— TTaoGaming
https://github.com/TTaoGaming
